chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Zurara, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a Name from the Names of Allah, when a man deletes it with his saliva. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Delete it with the cleanest of what you find.'

key_terms.الاسْم: The Name (specifically referring to the Names of Allah)

ai.seo_question: How should one erase the Names of Allah if they are written on paper or skin?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) addresses the practical etiquette of disposing of written Names of Allah, ruling that while erasing with saliva is permissible, one should ideally use the purest substance available, such as water. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *taharah* (purity) and reverence (*i'zim*) for the Divine Names, ensuring they are not treated with disrespect or mixed with impurities during disposal. The ruling underscores the principle that the method of removal should align with the highest standard of cleanliness accessible to the individual.
